conditions.text: Required setup, present in all three events: app version 3.2.0 on iOS 18.4, device model iPhone15,2.

Also present in all three events: push was deliverable, with OS permission ALLOWED and provider registration REGISTERED, and the profile was consistent; the packet does not say whether these matter to the crash, only that they held.
Not required: the specific entry action. The step before the crash varies across events between tapping button#load-more, tapping a.article-link, and foregrounding then navigating to /news/saved.
All support figures come from only three events, with one event per variant, so the preconditions are consistent but weakly sampled.

missing_evidence_questions.text: Do the three prefixes converge on a shared code path into loadPage, or are there genuinely three independent triggers?
Does the crash reproduce on app versions other than 3.2.0, on OS versions other than iOS 18.4, or on devices other than iPhone15,2 - or are those genuinely required?
Are the push and profile preconditions causally involved at all, or just incidental to these three sessions?
What state or input does loadPage see at line 88 when it throws - the packet gives the frame but no variable state or feed data.
Did the failure start appearing only after commit c32a444 shipped, which would strengthen or rule out that lead?
Are there more than three events for this incident that would show additional prefixes or break the 100% support of the preconditions?

steps_prose.text: Set up a session matching the recorded environment (see conditions) and then follow one of three observed two-step paths, each of which was seen in exactly one event.
Path A: navigate to /news, then tap button#load-more.
Path B: navigate to /news, then tap a.article-link.
Path C: bring the app to the foreground (LIFECYCLE foreground), then navigate to /news/saved.
In each path the crash is expected at the same place: the Error "Feed renderer crashed" thrown from loadPage in src/modules/news/feed.ts at line 88.

The three paths do not share a common prefix beyond all touching news screens, so the packet does not establish one single reproduction sequence; treat them as alternative routes to the same failure point.

As a lead only, commit c32a444 ("MEI-52: Local news feed paging") touches the same file as the culprit frame, src/modules/news/feed.ts, so exercising the paging code on that build is worth trying first; it is not established as the cause.

summary.text: Three events were analysed for an incident reported as Error: Feed renderer crashed, which surfaces in loadPage at src/modules/news/feed.ts line 88 after a short two-step interaction in the news section.
